title: Add design doc for handling unnamed artifact orphans

comments.body:
Thanks for sharing the document! I don't have enough Podman expertise to review the document as a whole, but I do wonder whether introducing the --replace option is the right direction. It seems like this would make the semantics of the image and artifact stores inconsistent, which could be surprising to users.

Is there a reason the artifact store could not behave the same way as the container image store? Operations on the image store can leave `<none>:<none>` and dangling objects behind. You can see them with `ls`, remove them with `rm`, and prune dangling objects with `prune`. As someone coming to the artifact store with experience using the image store, I would expect the same model.

Currently, if you pull a mutable artifact ref/tag that already exists locally but points to a different digest, the artifact store updates the local ref/tag and leaves the previous digest behind as a dangling (anonymous) object. I think this behavior is fine. I already understand that model from the image store, so it isn't surprising. What is surprising is that I can't `ls`, `rm`, or `prune` those dangling artifact digests. The `ls` and `rm` subcommands already exist, but currently don't work properly when the store contains dangling digests.

Ideally, `podman artifact ls` would let me see dangling artifact digests, either by default or through an additional option that enables extended output. `podman artifact rm` would then let me remove dangling artifacts by digest. The more closely this behavior matches `podman image ls` and `podman image rm`, the better IMO. Users coming to the artifact store from the image store have already internalized that model.

There also doesn't appear to be a way to prune dangling artifacts collectively. It would be useful to have that as well, analogous to `podman image prune`, although I don't think it's critical as long as `podman artifact rm` can remove individual dangling artifacts.

@janakj There was some discussion among the maintainers in a community call, and general sentiment was that we like the current behavior (no unnamed artifacts) and want to preserve it. In some ways, it simplifies matters considerably - reduces the need for pruning considerably because a pull won't create an unnamed and unused artifact, for example.
For reference, I haven't done an in-depth review, but the general approach of `--replace` required to overwrite and deleting unnamed artifacts on store init SGTM.

> @janakj There was some discussion among the maintainers in a community call, and general sentiment was that we like the current behavior (no unnamed artifacts) and want to preserve it. In some ways, it simplifies matters considerably - reduces the need for pruning considerably because a pull won't create an unnamed and unused artifact, for example.

@mheon I have always assumed pulls never destroy manifests and blobs that are in the local store already (image or artifact). This is convenient for digest pinning. If `podman artifact pull --replace` also deletes unnamed artifacts, then we can no longer assume pulls do not evict digests. Maybe that's fine, I don't know. But the operating models of the image and artifact stores diverge now, which is a bit unfortunate since they share almost everything else (ref format, digests, OCI registry infrastructure). I see how that simplifies the implementation, but wanted to point out the additional complexity at the user interface level.

Additionally, scripts and automations would most likely end up always using --replace. The alternative is to inspect the store first, but that is brittle, introduces race conditions, and complicates such scripts considerably. This could also get cumbersome with naturally mutable tags like latest.

If your consensus is not to support unnamed artifacts, I wonder if it might be more user friendly to preserve the repository name and remove the offending tag from the original digest when pulling. Then you would end up with the same configuration that pulling with `:@sha256...` already gives you, for example:

```
root@lima-dev:/home/janakj# podman artifact ls
REPOSITORY                             TAG         DIGEST        CREATED            SIZE
registry.example.com/artifact1  latest      0330ee97d085  About an hour ago  17.04kB
registry.example.com/artifact1              0330ee97d085  About an hour ago  17.04kB
registry.example.com/artifact1              0e47a2457cc8  About an hour ago  17.04kB
```

The benefit of this approach is that it does not introduce new flags or behavior. It is already supported by the current Podman version.

@janakj, your idea sounds interesting. I haven't looked into it deeply yet, but I think there might be some edge cases or undefined states. For example, handling multiple artifacts with the same name.

WDYT? @mtrmac, @baude

> Thanks for sharing the document! I don't have enough Podman expertise to review the document as a whole, but I do wonder whether introducing the --replace option is the right direction. It seems like this would make the semantics of the image and artifact stores inconsistent, which could be surprising to users.

I think users have gotten _used to_ the image store semantics, but it’s by no means _intuitive_.

It’s very weird that just running `podman build` + `podman push` for a few months eventually just runs out of disk space, and that users need to manage that manually.

It’s very weird that images have names, but sometimes (some situations, some APIs or outputs) that name is _the string_ `"<none>:<none>"`. How do I delete that? Well, by an image ID. Every image has an ID. No, wait, that’s actually  wrong, every _deduplicated_ image has an ID. (What is a deduplicated image? It’s _very_ complicated in some corner cases … and anyway Podman 6 has deprecated promising anything about it, by deprecating the promise of specific ID values.) Can I delete a named image that way? Well… kind of… but mostly no.

“Of course” changing the semantics of the image store is not on the table (well now that I said that…), but I think locking ourselves into that model for the artifact feature set is _not at all_ obviously desirable. Maybe we will need to expose artifact identity / reuse eventually for performance-sensitive use cases, but we seem not to be there yet, so I’d rather not lock ourselves into any specific performance-focused UX.

---

> Currently, if you pull a mutable artifact ref/tag that already exists locally but points to a different digest, the artifact store updates the local ref/tag and leaves the previous digest behind as a dangling (anonymous) object. I think this behavior is fine.

What good does the unnamed object do? With images, they at least serve as a build cache. Here we are left with … “the user explicitly removed/replaced that artifact but we have left the files around in case users change their minds and want to pull it again”. That’s not compelling to me.

> `podman artifact rm` would then let me remove dangling artifacts by digest.

If we are talking about exposing internals of the kind digests are: The store does internally not work that way: it has one top-level manifest _per name_, so if we pull an exactly identical artifact under three tags, and remove them all, we are left with _three_ unnamed objects _with the same digest_.

I’m sure we could figure out an UX for deleting “the second one of the three”, but… why would anyone want to manage things at that level of detail?

On the contrary: I think we’d, at least for now, like the freedom to change how the storage system works, so that we can, perhaps, change this behavior. (I’m not at all saying there are plans to do that, nor that it should be a priority short-term; just that locking ourselves into what `c/image/oci/layout` has chosen to do, semantics chosen for ~unrelated use cases, seems unnecessary.)

---

> @mheon I have always assumed pulls never destroy manifests and blobs that are in the local store already (image or artifact). This is convenient for digest pinning. 

If you want to refer to an artifact by repo@digest at runtime, pull it by repo@digest in the first place. That makes it _not unnamed_; it is named with a repo@digest.

> If `podman artifact pull --replace` also deletes unnamed artifacts, then we can no longer assume pulls do not evict digests. Maybe that's fine, I don't know. But the operating models of the image and artifact stores diverge now

I don’t see this substantially different from images: An _unnamed image_ cannot be referenced using the repo@digest syntax either, because it has no repo to match against. Digest references only work for images pulled by digest (= named with the digest), or pulled by some other tag within the same repo where that other tag was not removed; they don’t work for images where pulling an updated tag has made them completely unnamed.

(I would also find it operationally very problematic to have unnamed objects, such that `podman image ls` or `podman artifact ls` shows no identity apart from a hex string, which some other deployment configuration requires to exist. How would a sysadmin on such a system know what to delete / what workload to attribute that disk space to?)

---

> Additionally, scripts and automations would most likely end up always using --replace.

Yes, I think that’s a good argument against making that option required.

> If your consensus is not to support unnamed artifacts, I wonder if it might be more user friendly to preserve the repository name and remove the offending tag from the original digest when pulling. Then you would end up with the same configuration that pulling with `:@sha256...` already gives you, for example:
> 
> ```
> root@lima-dev:/home/janakj# podman artifact ls
> REPOSITORY                             TAG         DIGEST        CREATED            SIZE
> registry.example.com/artifact1  latest      0330ee97d085  About an hour ago  17.04kB
> registry.example.com/artifact1              0330ee97d085  About an hour ago  17.04kB
> registry.example.com/artifact1              0e47a2457cc8  About an hour ago  17.04kB
> ```

If the proposal is that 
```
podman artifact pull repo:latest # digestA
# tag moves
podman artifact pull repo:latest # digestB
```
should end up as the equivalent of
```
podman artifact pull repo@digestA
podman artifact pull repo:latest # digestB
```
(i.e. when the tag updates, keep the old artifact around, don’t delete it), yes, that’s a possible semantics.

I think it would be _highly_ unintuitive; most users pull repo:tag because they want to use exactly that, not repo@digest (if they wanted repo@digest, it would be natural to pull repo@digest in the first place!), and fairly likely for precisely one use. Those users would be accumulating old versions of the moving-tag artifacts that they probably don’t want.
